youtube.title: Ocarina of Time Sold 5.2 Million in 4 Days on Switch 2
youtube.description: The Ocarina of Time remake is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published Switch 2 game over its first four days, and the $520 Zelda console that launched alongside it doesn't include a copy. Here's what that means for your wallet and which one we'd actually buy. Sources: Insider Gaming, Eurogamer, GameSpot, with sales data from Nintendo and Circana's Mat Piscatella.

claims.claim: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 sold over 5.2 million units worldwide in its first four days after launching November 5, 2026, according to Nintendo.
That is the highest global sales for any Nintendo-published Switch 2 game in its first four days.
Circana's Mat Piscatella said Switch 2 had its best US dollar sales week of 2026 so far, thanks to the 40th Anniversary Edition console.
The Legend of Zelda: 40th Anniversary Edition Switch 2 console costs $520 and does not include a copy of the game.
The game is priced at $60 digitally and $70 on a physical cartridge.
The remake is the highest-rated video game of 2026.

issues.quote: the $520 Zelda console that launched alongside it
issues.problem: The sources say the console launched on October 29 and the game on November 5, a week apart. GameSpot does say the console 'debuted with the game', so 'alongside' is loose rather than unsupported.

issues.quote: gave Switch 2 its best US sales week of twenty twenty-six
issues.problem: The sources say it was the best week of 2026 'so far' and measured in dollar sales. The script drops both qualifiers, though the on-screen card does specify dollar sales.
The prices match GameSpot, but '(region Switch 2)' is unclear wording and looks like a template artefact. The sources give these as US dollar prices.

check.summary: Pass: every factual claim is supported by the sources, with three minor wording issues. The 5.2 million units in four days and the Nintendo-published Switch 2 four-day record come from Nintendo via Insider Gaming. The best US dollar sales week of 2026, attributed to Circana, and the $520 console without the game are in Eurogamer and GameSpot. The $60 digital and $70 physical prices are in GameSpot, and the highest-rated game of 2026 claim is in Insider Gaming. The 1998 N64 release is established public knowledge, and the buying advice is clearly framed as opinion. Nothing is rumour, so the non-rumour label is correct.
